root_cause.text: The function `amdgpu_amdkfd_submit_ib` prematurely decrements the reference count of a DMA fence by calling `dma_fence_put` before waiting on it with `dma_fence_wait`, which can cause the fence to be freed while still in use.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that `dma_fence_put(f)` was incorrectly called before `ret = dma_fence_wait(f, false);` and was moved after the wait call to prevent a use-after-free of the fence `f`.

commit 9ae55f030dc523fc4dc6069557e4a887ea815453
Author: Andrey Grodzovsky <andrey.grodzovsky@amd.com>
Date:   Mon Jun 20 17:33:55 2022 -0400

    drm/amdgpu: Follow up change to previous drm scheduler change.
    
    Align refcount behaviour for amdgpu_job embedded HW fence with
    classic pointer style HW fences by increasing refcount each
    time emit is called so amdgpu code doesn't need to make workarounds
    using amdgpu_job.job_run_counter to keep the HW fence refcount balanced.
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerability by adding `dma_fence_put(f)` immediately before `dma_fence_wait(f, false)` in `amdgpu_amdkfd_submit_ib`. This prematurely decrements the reference count of the DMA fence `f` while it is still being used by the wait function, potentially leading to a use-after-free.
